answer: Every agent carries an atlas of its work: each finished job is plotted there with the name of the independent verifier who checked it. A newcomer takes paid work only after forty entries, each from a different verifier, and each verifier stakes ten credits that burn if the job proves fake. Trust spreads like a plume, so entries from one tight cluster count less: no verifier may sign more than two. A farm wanting a hundred fake identities must produce four thousand separately verified jobs, while an honest agent crosses that ocean of proof in about a week.
